ios.desc:
Battery Life shows the battery level of your iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, AirPods and other connected devices in one place – in the app, in widgets and on your watch face. Downloaded by millions of users since 2014.

► BATTERY
• Battery charge in percent, charging state, thermal state and Low Power Mode
• Runtimes: how long the remaining charge lasts for video, video streaming, audio, web browsing and more, based on the figures Apple publishes for your model
• Battery health: the real maximum capacity, charge cycles and battery condition of your iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch, read from the analytics files iOS writes

► CONNECTED DEVICES
• AirPods and their charging case, Beats, keyboards, trackpads, game controllers, hearing aids and other accessories that report their battery over Bluetooth or cable
• The last reading stays visible after a device disconnects
• Give devices your own names and hide the ones you do not need

► WIDGETS (iOS 17 or later)
• Three widgets in different sizes for your Home Screen: Battery, Runtimes and Devices
• Lock Screen widgets for a glance without unlocking
• Pick the device to show, your favorite accessories and the sort order

► NOTIFICATIONS
• Get notified when your iPhone, iPad or Apple Watch has charged to the level you choose
• Get notified when a battery falls below the level you choose

► APPLE WATCH (watchOS 10 or later)
• The Watch app shows the battery level of your Apple Watch, your iPhone and your connected devices
• Complications for any watch face: Watch battery, iPhone battery or both

► BATTERY LIFE PRO (one-time In-App Purchase)
• No advertisements
• All notifications, including low battery and Apple Watch
• The larger Runtimes and Devices widgets
• Connected devices and raw data in the Watch app, plus the iPhone and combined complications
• Battery health charts, the full history of readings and more figures
• Sync your battery health readings with iCloud

► PRIVACY
Your battery readings and your list of devices stay on your device. There are no accounts. If you switch on Sync with iCloud (Pro), your battery health readings are kept in your own iCloud account, which only you can see.

► PLEASE NOTE
iOS and watchOS decide how often an app may run in the background. Notifications, widgets and complications therefore update on a schedule set by the system, usually every 5 to 60 minutes, and cannot show real-time values. Notifications need Background App Refresh, and they stop when the app is closed in the App Swi
